question: What is the importance of the ozone layer for life on Earth?

options.text: It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.
It protects us from acidic rainfall.

solution:
The correct answer is **__It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ozone layer is one of the layers in the earth's atmosphere inside the stratosphere layer. It absorbs ultraviolet radiation and protects people, animals, plants, and marine life from the sun's harmful rays.
 
• It was discovered by** Charles Fabry and Henri Buisson in 1913.**
 
• It can** absorb 98% of the sun's ultraviolet rays and almost 90% of ozone is located in the stratosphere layer at a distance of 15 to 30 km from the surface of Earth.**
 
• **In 1989, the Montreal protocol **came to protect the ozone layer by cutting the substances that deplete the ozone layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone:**

 
 
• It is important to mankind because it creates a protective coverage against ultraviolet rays.
 
• **Formula Ozone is O₃.**
 
• The ozone layer is found in the stratosphere. The stratosphere is the mass of protective gases clinging to our planet. The ozone layer acts as a shield for life on Earth.
 
• The ozone layer only makes **up 0.00006 per cent **of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• The ozone layer is getting thinner because of chemicals called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). Due to this reason nowadays hydrochlorofluorocarbons **(HCFCs) are used in place of CFCs.**
 
• **CFCs are non-toxic, nonflammable chemicals containing atoms of carbon, chlorine, and fluorine.**
 
• **"Ozone holes”** are popular names for areas of damage to the ozone layer.
 
• **The ozone layer is thinnest near the poles due to very low temperatures.**
